subject.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these owner-only conversation tools and the same-v11 persistence model as permanent core contracts?
rationale: This adds public model-facing tools, Gateway protocol methods, durable state, and a migration policy that cannot be accepted solely from implementation correctness or green automated checks.

options.title: Adopt after proof
options.body: Accept the core architecture and same-v11 released-upgrade policy after conflicts and real Reef proof are resolved.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land only conversation discovery and fire-and-forget send, deferring correlated turns and their durable reply state.

options.title: Keep transport-specific
options.body: Reject the new core contract and continue using explicit message-channel targets or plugin-owned coordination.

recommendation.title: Adopt after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the core architecture and same-v11 released-upgrade policy after conflicts and real Reef proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and broad ownership across the affected runtime, persistence, and Reef surfaces make this the strongest available decision owner.
